paragraph: You can't buy that at the local **convenience** store. Their union is based on mutual benefit and **convenience**. It started raining on my way to the **convenience** store.
english: the quality of being convenient

paragraph: The cat is on the **mat**. In passing, we wiped our feet on the **mat**. There was a welcome **mat** in front of the door.
english: a flat piece of coarse material used for wiping one’s feet, or as a decorative or protective floor covering

paragraph: That threw **adequate** light on his feelings toward her. We need not only **adequate** water but clean water. I believe our imagination isn't quite **adequate** to picture it.
english: equal to or fulfilling some requirement

paragraph: I thought the **brass** section was a little off. What's the easiest **brass** instrument to learn to play? The color of gold is very similar to **brass**.
english: a metallic alloy of copper and zinc used in many industrial and plumbing applications

paragraph: In France, a lot of cars run on **diesel**. The truck is powered by a **diesel** engine. Could you help me by sending **diesel**?
english: a vehicle powered by a diesel engine

paragraph: Smoking reduces the **effectiveness** of the immune system. Don't doubt the **effectiveness** of this medicine. Don't mix up **effectiveness** and efficiency.
english: how well something works

paragraph: I like this television. The sound is **exceptional**. He is good, not to say **exceptional**. I want to be an **exceptional** teacher.
english: forming an exception

paragraph: Saying what you think **frankly** is not a bad thing. **Frankly** speaking, I don't agree with you. **Frankly** speaking, he is wrong.
english: in a frank, open or (too) honest manner
arabicDesc: مثال: قول ما تفكر فيه بصراحة ليس أمرًا سيئًا.

paragraph: Say no to **hatred** and violence. I have a large **hatred** of the foot race. There is still serious racial **hatred** against black people.
english: strong aversion
arabicDesc: مثال: قُل لا للكراهية و العنف.

paragraph: Nobody is thought to be **ignorant** of the law. You know everybody is **ignorant**, only on different subjects. He is rude and **ignorant** and people avoid him.
english: unknowledgeable or uneducated

paragraph: Your **Majesty**, there is a fire in my house! He carries himself with the **majesty** of a king. Shall we proceed to the throne room, Your **Majesty**?
english: the quality of being impressive, great, dignified, powerful, sovereign, or any combination thereof

paragraph: It is important to know the difference between mean and **median**.
english: a line segment joining the vertex of triangle to the midpoint of the opposing side

paragraph: My major is **medieval** European history. His mother is a noted **medieval** Chinese literature specialist. I was deeply impressed with the **medieval** music.
english: from the Middle Ages
arabicDesc: مثال: تخصصي هو تاريخ أوروبا في العصور الوسطى.

paragraph: This area is reserved for people with reduced **mobility**. Social **mobility** does not exist in this country. The concept of social **mobility** is a lie.
english: the ability to move

paragraph: I want to go to America **someday**. You'll forget about me **someday**. I don't know whether I'll be a dad **someday**.
english: sometime; at some time in the future
arabicDesc: مثال: أريد الذهاب إلى أمريكا يوماً من الأيام.

paragraph: I bought a **sophisticated** security system for my house. The engineer demonstrated how to operate the **sophisticated** system. I think it's a little more **sophisticated** than that.
english: to make more complex or refined (usually sophisticated)

paragraph: You can't access an instance variable from a **static** method. House prices have remained **static** for several months. The **static** electricity started to make our hair stand on end.
english: not moving or changing

paragraph: The women are very **supportive**. I think you should be a little more **supportive**. She dedicated her service award to her **supportive** team.
english: giving help and encouragement

paragraph: Without water, **surgical** procedures and infection control become challenging. In alert hands, the vote can be an effective **surgical** instrument. How common are **surgical** errors?
english: of, relating to, used in, or resulting from surgery

paragraph: The US is regularly defeated in conventional **warfare**. The two countries are engaged in biological **warfare**. We live in a time of psychological **warfare**.
english: fighting in a war

paragraph: The soldiers headed for the **frontier** with caution. Many families left to make a new life on the **frontier**. We crossed the **frontier** yesterday.
english: the part of a country which borders or faces another country or unsettled region

paragraph: Would you please **chew** up my food for me? It's really rude to **chew** with your mouth open. You know you should **chew** thoroughly and then swallow!
english: to crush with the teeth by repeated closing and opening of the jaws

paragraph: The police spotted him at once as the **offender**. He even suspected that the man was the principal **offender**. The political **offender** rebelled against the police authority.
english: one who gives or causes offense, or does something wrong

paragraph: She's watering the **lawn**, isn't she? The **lawn** needs to be watered. They are sitting on the **lawn** and the ground.
english: ground (generally in front of or around a house) covered with grass kept closely mown
arabicDesc: مثال: هي تسقي العشب، أليس كذلك؟

paragraph: His **resignation** as Prime Minister came as a surprise. They were stunned after finding out about his **resignation**. The company appealed for people to take voluntary **resignation**.
english: the act of resigning

paragraph: There are three cows in the **barn**. The dog and cat are sleeping in the **barn**. The **barn** collapsed under the weight of the snow.
english: a building, often found on a farm, used for storage or keeping animals such as cattle
arabicDesc: مثال: هناك ثلاثة أبقار في الإسطبل.

paragraph: She telephoned her best friend to vent her **frustration**. People react to the **frustration** in much the same way. Try to turn your **frustration** into an opportunity.
english: the feeling of annoyance at impossibility from resistance or inability to achieve something

paragraph: Who said cross **stitch** is strictly for women only? I haven't done a **stitch** of work today. I just bought three new cross **stitch** kits.
english: a single pass of a needle in sewing

paragraph: Life is one **awakening** after the other. Wake up early to **awaken** your fortune. This book will **awaken** your imagination.
english: to cause to become awake
arabicDesc: مثال: الحياة نهضة واحدة تلو الأخرى.

paragraph: What's the **width** of this road? The belt has a **width** of about one span. What is the height, length and **width** of the container?
english: measurement of something from side to side

paragraph: Scientists have discovered a new species of **dinosaur**. He was accused of stealing **dinosaur** bones. The new **dinosaur** exhibit is cool.
english: a large reptile that lived long ago
arabicDesc: مثال: اكتشف العلماء أنواعا جديدة من الدينصورات.

paragraph: He would pay a million dollars for such a **specimen**. This is a very rare **specimen**. My private library consists of more than a thousand **specimens**.
english: a sample for study

paragraph: Do you have any **cement**? The **cement** will set in a couple of hours. I fixed the hole in the wall with **cement**.
english: a powdered substance

paragraph: She plans to resume playing soon in the **orchestra**. The performance by the community **orchestra** was a delight. He wants a full **orchestra** for his wedding.
english: a large group of musicians who play together on various instruments, usually including some from strings, woodwind, brass and/or percussion

paragraph: The **frost** had a bad effect on the crops. The beautiful garden was completely wrecked by the **frost**. All the early flowers were bitten by the **frost**.
english: the cold weather that causes these ice crystals to form

other.meaning: cold weather that would cause frost

paragraph: Nobody intends to **erect** a wall. Sit **erect** and sit still. He held the flag **erect**.
english: to build; standing straight up

paragraph: I have made a **vow** never to get married. The **vow** of a lover is not taken seriously. The monk took a **vow** of silence.
english: a declaration or assertion

paragraph: A drowning man will **clutch** at a straw. He slowly let the **clutch** out and drove off. The truck had some issues with the **clutch**.
english: to hold tightly; a pedal in a car

paragraph: All the common electric lamps (less than 70 **watts**) are made with vacuums inside.
english: in the International System of Units, the derived unit of power

paragraph: The second **accusation** was that we were bad patriots. I can't find any evidence to support your **accusation**. It was a classic case of **accusation** in a mirror.
english: the act of accusing

other.meaning: that of which one is accused

paragraph: A man on a quest to **empower** the world. My goal is to help you **empower** yourself. He seeks to **empower** others through learning.
english: to give power or confidence

paragraph: It's an old-fashioned **variant**. What features do the different **variants** have in common? Apparently, both **variants** were considered correct in 2016.
english: something that is slightly different from a type or norm

paragraph: We only serve the prime **rib** dinner on weekends. I think I have a broken **rib**. Our neighbor has broken a **rib**.
english: any of a series of long curved bones occurring in 12 pairs in humans and other animals and extending from the spine to or toward the sternum

paragraph: Noise-canceling headphones are designed to **suppress** background sounds. I wonder how I can **suppress** this feeling. The government tried to **suppress** the protests by increasing security.
english: to stop by force; to hide a feeling

paragraph: Dreams help to **consolidate** knowledge gained during the day. We need to **consolidate** the access control code. They continued to **consolidate** their leadership position in that space.
english: to make stronger; to combine

paragraph: I really hope that I can speak **authentic** Chinese. Self-acceptance is the basis of an **authentic** life. Where can I find an **authentic** food restaurant?
english: real; not fake

paragraph: You started pushing me **backwards**. Bend over **backwards** for him and he still complain. Everything is going **backwards** a bit at a time.
english: toward the back

paragraph: Everything around that abandoned mansion just gave **creepy** vibes. I don't want to watch this film. It's **creepy**! The guy had a **creepy** look on his face.
english: moving by creeping along

paragraph: On-again, off-again relationships can be **emotionally** draining. I'll stay **emotionally** distant to protect my heart. Seeing myself getting older is upsetting me **emotionally**.
english: in terms of feelings

paragraph: It was a wonderful **finale**.
english: the grand end of something, especially of a show or piece of music

paragraph: If you think education is expensive, wait till you see what **ignorance** costs you. They got into the grip of **ignorance** and poverty. He pretended **ignorance**, which made me still more angry.
english: condition of being uninformed or uneducated
arabicDesc: مثال: إن كنت تظن التعليم مكلفًا، فانتظر حتى ترى ما يكلفك الجهل.

paragraph: As people like honey, so **likewise** do bears. The exit is **likewise** on the ground floor. **Likewise**, it was nice to meet you.
english: in a similar manner
arabicDesc: كلمات قريبة: أيضا، على حد سواء، بالمثل

paragraph: The view from the top of that building was **magnificent**. Aside from that, I found our weekend quite **magnificent**. Have you honestly ever seen a view so **magnificent**?
english: grand, elegant or splendid in appearance
arabicDesc: مثال: كان المنظر من قمة هذا المبنى رائعا.

paragraph: He is involved in working out the **mathematical** problem. He is good at solving complicated **mathematical** problems. In my country there is a shocking amount of **mathematical** ignorance.
english: of, or relating to mathematics

paragraph: What are you going to do in the **meantime**? In the **meantime**, the main problem has not disappeared. You can have a snack in the **meantime**.
english: the time between two events

paragraph: They won the game, but have been eliminated **nonetheless**. One should never laugh on that. **Nonetheless** she laughed. It was already late, but she left **nonetheless**.
english: however; despite this

paragraph: We decided to bike to a nearby **recreation** park. Every now and then, I play tennis for **recreation**. What do you do for **recreation** around here?
english: any activity, such as play, that amuses, diverts or stimulates

paragraph: The last time I went to China, I visited **Shanghai**. For how long are you in **Shanghai**? I left **Shanghai** last year and have not yet been back.
english: a large city in China
arabicDesc: مثال: زرتُ شانغهاي لَمَّا زرتُ الصين المرة الأخيرة.

paragraph: We went out in **spite** of the rain. He never says thanks in **spite** of all that I've done for him. In **spite** of everything, I think it's not bad.
english: ill will or hatred toward another, accompanied with the desire to unjustifiably irritate, annoy, or thwart
arabicDesc: مثال: خرجنا بالرغم من هطول المطر.

paragraph: It was the day before **Thanksgiving**. The calendar doesn't have the correct date for **Thanksgiving**. I hope that I can spend **Thanksgiving** with you.
english: thanksgiving Day
arabicDesc: مثال: كان ذلك عشيّة عيد الشّكر.

paragraph: The men can visit the **thermal** baths after noon. The atomic reactor generates enormous amounts of **thermal** energy. These **thermal** socks will keep your feet warm.
english: relating to heat

paragraph: Which prince is the legitimate **heir** to the throne? Being an only child, he was the sole **heir**. Ill-gotten goods thrive not to the third **heir**.
english: someone who inherits, or is designated to inherit, the property of another

other.meaning: one who inherits, or has been designated to inherit, a hereditary title or office

paragraph: Simply put, a human being is an **aggregate** of many cells.
english: a mass, assemblage, or sum of particulars

other.meaning: any of the five aspects constituting the sentient being in Buddhism

paragraph: The government tortured the civilian to get a **confession**. How long has it been since your last **confession**? I'm afraid I have a **confession** to make.
english: the open admittance of having done something (especially something bad)

other.meaning: disclosure of one's sins to a priest

paragraph: To say so should not **diminish** his importance. Our unique traits should not **diminish** our respect for one another. This inner conflict tends to **diminish** as the years go by.
english: to make smaller

paragraph: The snake is the symbol of the **pharmaceutical** industry. This laboratory belongs to a respected **pharmaceutical** company. The **pharmaceutical** company is located nearby.
english: relating to medicines

paragraph: I can't **tolerate** this noise any longer. His pride wouldn't allow him to **tolerate** such insults. I won't **tolerate** those kinds of insults from anyone.
english: to allow or permit without explicit approval, usually if it is perceived as negative
arabicDesc: مثال: لا أستطيع تحمل هذا الضجيج أكثر من ذلك.

paragraph: The gang was planning a **robbery**. The taxi driver has an involvement in the **robbery**. He was in prison on a charge of **robbery**.
english: act or practice of robbing

paragraph: I would rather have a sandwich than a **toast**. He put a lot of honey on his **toast**. Some buttered **toast** floated in the hot chicken soup.
english: bread browned by heat; a drink to honor someone

paragraph: I myself was a **missionary** in Africa. My favorite position is **missionary**. I don't like door-to-door **missionaries**.
english: one who is sent on a mission

paragraph: He watches for an opportunity to **intrigue** against his rival. This is a very interesting, **intriguing**, and compelling story. I'm **intrigued** to know what you think it means.
english: a complicated or clandestine plot or scheme intended to effect some purpose by secret artifice

paragraph: They're either in the shed or in the **den**. The foxes are in their **den**. He found a bear **den**.
english: a small cavern or hollow place in the side of a hill, or among rocks

paragraph: I think they should **repeal** that law. We request that they **repeal** this law. We demand the **repeal** of this law.
english: to officially end a law

paragraph: We must **prevail** against our rivals by all means. No matter what it takes we must **prevail**. It's time for our better angels to **prevail**.
english: to be superior in strength, dominance, influence, or frequency

paragraph: If he were a **bachelor**, I would marry him. He remained a **bachelor** throughout his life. That man is definitely a **bachelor**.
english: a person, especially a man, who is socially regarded as able to marry but has not yet

paragraph: I think that Islam is an **amazing** religion. My math teacher is **amazing**. There is nothing that can **amaze** my dad.
english: to fill (someone) with surprise and wonder
arabicDesc: مثال: أعتقد أن الإسلام دين رائع.

paragraph: I'm tired of listening to his **boasts**. It's not a thing one can well **boast** of. If not a lie, close to a **boast**.
english: a brag
arabicDesc: مثال: سئمت من تحمل تباهيه بنفسه.

paragraph: I like water with orange **peel**. I can **peel** an apple. I like to **peel** apples.
english: to remove skin

other.meaning: The skin or outer layer of a fruit, vegetable, etc (noun)

paragraph: Water has two hydrogen **atoms** and one oxygen **atom**. Iron Arm **Atom** protected the country from danger. There is one electron in a hydrogen **atom**.
english: a hypothetical particle posited by Greek philosophers as an ultimate and indivisible component of matter

paragraph: He went out with him on the **rebound**. Happiness, I have discovered, is nearly always a **rebound** from hard work. Since then, the economy has slowly **rebounded**.
english: to bounce back; to recover

paragraph: These bear **cubs** are still nursing. A female bear could be very dangerous, especially when her **cubs** are around. In the first months of their lives, bear **cubs** are completely dependent on their mothers.
english: the young of certain animals, chiefly large carnivorous mammals, including the bear, wolf, fox, lion and tiger
arabicDesc: مثال: لا يزال جروي الدّب هذيه يرضعان.

paragraph: He was a **fixture** at the local mosque. She's a **fixture** at all the high-society parties. He was called to fix a broken light **fixture**.
english: something fixed in a building; a sports event
arabicDesc: مثال: كان يتواجد دائما في المسجد المحلّي.

paragraph: This death left a deep **void** in my heart. The beach was completely **void** of any other people. The separation left a **void** in his life.
english: an empty space; not legally valid

paragraph: I have a **sore** throat and a slight fever. Do you have a headache and a **sore** throat? My arm is very **sore** where you hit me.
english: causing pain or discomfort

other.meaning: An injured, infected, inflamed or diseased patch of skin (noun)

paragraph: Most countries around the world use the **metric** system. Conversion to the **metric** system was opposed by tool manufacturers. The **metric** system is a universal system of weights and measures.
english: of or relating to the metric system of measurement

paragraph: Your room is **cleaner** than mine. Have you bought a vacuum **cleaner** yet or not? Our streets look **cleaner** than they used to.
english: a person whose occupation is to clean things, especially rooms, floors, and windows

paragraph: Her income puts her into the highest tax **bracket**. In my age **bracket**, there are no job offers available. The highest German income tax **bracket** begins at a relatively low income.
english: a fixture attached to a wall to hold up a shelf

other.meaning: one of several ranges of numbers

paragraph: My father will retire at the age of **sixty**. Ask a six-year-old, not a **sixty**-year-old. There are **sixty** seconds in a minute.
english: cardinal number
arabicDesc: مثال: سيتقاعد أبي في سن الستين.

paragraph: There was a long **interval** before he replied. How many minutes does the **interval** last? The **interval** lasts for ten minutes.
english: a distance in space

paragraph: Do you have any **objection** to this plan? He brought forward a strong **objection** to my proposal. We have no **objection** to you joining our club.
english: act of objecting
arabicDesc: مثال: هل عندك اعتراض على هذه الخطة.

paragraph: This **enzyme** is produced in the stomach. The **enzymes** break down food.
english: leavened bread, as opposed to azyme

paragraph: I really think we can **oversee** this. Tom is in charge of **overseeing** the entire project.
english: to survey, look at something in a wide angle

paragraph: I want those responsible for the **massacre** brought to trial. Did you hear about the **massacre**? There was a **massacre**, and we didn't have enough courage to intervene.
english: any overwhelming defeat, as in a game or sport

other.meaning: To win against (an opponent) very decisively (verb)

paragraph: He has decided to go on the **wagon**. Pull over and let the meat **wagon** pass. You are the fifth wheel on the **wagon**.
english: a heavier four-wheeled (normally horse-drawn) vehicle designed to carry goods (or sometimes people)

paragraph: Do you think there will be a **coup**? He took power in a military **coup**. Prosecuting those who attempted a **coup** is not a witch hunt.
english: a sudden illegal takeover of a government

paragraph: The **raven** wouldn't dare do this with an eagle. Why is a **raven** like a writing-desk? A **raven** is as black as coal.
english: any of several, generally large, species of birds in the genus Corvus with lustrous black plumage

paragraph: He is the last person to **betray** his friends. By giving up on your dreams, you **betray** yourself. He wastes his life, forgetting to **betray** his organization.
english: to deliver into the hands of an enemy by treachery or fraud, in violation of trust

paragraph: Why do you want to buy a back **brace**? Don't use a back **brace** for a muscle strain. She has a **brace** on her right leg.
english: to prepare for something bad; a support

paragraph: On the great **vault** of this cathedral, we feel very small. Employees of the bank hid from the active shooter in the **vault**. Your **vaulting** ambitions are clouding your judgment.
english: an arched masonry structure supporting and forming a ceiling, whether freestanding or forming part of a larger building

paragraph: I'm looking for something to **vent** my anger on. The sound was coming from inside the **vent**. I don't have anyone to **vent** to.
english: an opening through which gases, especially air, can pass
